active_product_bottleneck.observation: Actual Builder preserves >9.33 MB Office saving, but corrected real parallel staging misses the frozen 1.25x create ceiling (10790261113: 1.28531x). Safe physical-only mode1 is fast (10790625860: create 1.10040x, extract 0.85783x, RSS 1.00x) but saves only 5,651,816 B, retaining 60.55% of the breakthrough. A direct authenticated-physical-record rewrite cannot fix that byte loss by itself: the charged five-winner cohort contains 9,450,199 B of exact Deflate payload before any record/Merkle/index overhead, already far above the ~6.11 MB archive implied by the 9.334 MB breakthrough. The missing compression comes from shared logical reconstruction, not authentication metadata.
active_product_bottleneck.next_discriminator: Do not build a direct r25 physical-record clone of mode1. Test a representation that compresses/reconstructs the physical Deflate streams themselves from shared information, or move the expensive logical reconstruction boundary into a materially faster implementation while preserving the existing >9 MB byte owner.

primary_question.hypothesis: Exact Deflate streams can be represented from a smaller shared basis/residual or reconstructed through a faster bounded implementation so CMPCT retains the >9 MB logical-sharing gain without the current Python create debt.
primary_question.kill: A physical-stream representation must beat the 9.45 MB direct-payload floor materially enough to approach the current ~6.11 MB candidate while keeping exactness/locality bounded; an execution-boundary intervention must cross 1.25x on the unchanged product gate. Do not award credit to authentication-only repackaging.
